## Discordant Imaging and Pathology

Observed facts: The patient has a documented history of follicular lymphoma progressing to high-grade B-cell lymphoma with MYC, BCL2, and BCL6 alterations and marrow involvement, treated with R-mini-CHOP. Post-treatment imaging shows a mixed response with new liver lesions. The liver biopsy expresses histiocytic/dendritic markers rather than B-cell markers. MYC and BCL2 abnormalities in the liver material overlap with the earlier lymphoma. Clonality testing on the original follicular lymphoma was not completed.

Hypotheses (not established): The overlap of MYC and BCL2 alterations between the liver lesion and the prior B-cell lymphoma raises the possibility of a clonal relationship, but this is not proven. The histiocytic/dendritic immunophenotype in the liver does not fit a B-cell lymphoma recurrence and could represent a reactive process, a histiocytic/dendritic neoplasm, or a transformation not yet characterised. The material does not securely establish a single histiocytic/dendritic subtype.

Proposed actions: Expert haematopathology review comparing the liver biopsy with the original lymphoma sections, including full immunohistochemistry panel and morphologic correlation. Completion of clonality studies (e.g., IgH/TCR rearrangement) on both the original follicular lymphoma and the liver material to test for shared clonality. Consideration of additional molecular studies (e.g., BRAF V600E, MAP2K1, or other histiocytic-associated mutations) if the histiocytic/dendritic phenotype is confirmed, to aid subtyping. Multidisciplinary tumour board discussion integrating imaging, pathology, and clinical context before determining management.
